classification.difficultyReason: Form two cost equations and eliminate the unrequested item price by multiplying both equations.

content.prompt:
Solve this problem by introducing two pronumerals and forming two simultaneous equations, even though it may be done more easily using one pronumeral.

Romeo spends $\$15.60$ and buys 3 hamburgers and 5 buckets of chips. Manni spends $\$12.40$ and buys 4 hamburgers and 2 buckets of chips. How much does a hamburger cost?

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the cost of a hamburger in dollars and $y$ be the cost of a bucket of chips in dollars.

$$\begin{align*}3x+5y&=15.60 &&(1)\\4x+2y&=12.40 &&(2)\end{align*}$$

Eliminate $y$:

$$\begin{align*}6x+10y&=31.20 &&(1)\times2\\20x+10y&=62.00 &&(2)\times5\\14x&=30.80 &&\text{subtract}\\x&=2.20\end{align*}$$

Therefore a hamburger costs $\$2.20$.

Check: substituting $x=2.20$ into (2) gives $y=1.80$. Then $3(2.20)+5(1.80)=15.60$ and $4(2.20)+2(1.80)=12.40$.
